subject: Literature
title: The Tale of Genji and Eastern Narrative
description: A 60-second lesson on The Tale of Genji and Eastern Narrative.

hook.text: Around the year 1000, a Japanese court lady wrote what many scholars consider the world's first novel.

buildup.text: Murasaki Shikibu's The Tale of Genji explored love, loss, and politics in the imperial court of Heian Japan.

discovery.text: The novel featured deep psychological realism and complex character development centuries before Europe.

twist.text: Because women were barred from writing in formal Chinese characters, Shikibu wrote in Japanese phonetic script.

climax.text: The Tale of Genji proved that restriction can fuel creativity, as the constraint produced a masterpiece.

punchline.text: A woman banned from formal writing invented the novel.

quiz.question: Why did Murasaki Shikibu write in Japanese phonetic script?
options: Women were barred from writing in formal Chinese characters
Phonetic script was the only script that existed
